title: Orifice Discharge — Free Flow Under Gate

Cd.description: Discharge coefficient (0.55–0.72 depending on gate type)

H.description: Effective upstream head above center of opening

applicability: For free (unsubmerged) discharge where downstream water level is below the gate opening. When tailwater submerges the opening, use submerged orifice equation.

title: Submerged Orifice Discharge

Cd.description: Discharge coefficient (slightly lower than free flow)

applicability: When tailwater submerges the gate opening. Applicable to slide gates, radial gates operating under submerged conditions, and conduit gates.

title: Hydrostatic Force on Flat Gate

F.description: Total hydrostatic force on gate face

h_c.description: Depth from water surface to centroid of gate

applicability: For vertical flat gates. Center of pressure: y_cp = y_c + I_c/(y_c × A), where I_c = second moment of area about centroidal axis. For rectangular gate: y_cp = y_c + d²/12 / y_c.

title: Radial (Tainter) Gate — Resultant Hydrostatic Force

F_V.description: Vertical component = γ × Volume of water above curved surface

F_R.description: Resultant force — passes through trunnion center for circular arc

applicability: For a circular arc gate, the resultant of all hydrostatic pressure forces passes through the center of the arc (trunnion). This means hoist force only needs to overcome gate weight, seal friction, and trunnion friction — NOT hydrostatic load.

title: Slide Gate Hoist Force
equation: F_hoist = W × sin(θ) + μ_seal × F_seal + μ_guide × F_guide + F_downpull

F_hoist.description: Required hoist force to open gate

θ.description: Gate inclination from horizontal (90° for vertical)

F_seal.description: Normal force on seals from hydrostatic pressure

F_downpull.description: Hydrodynamic downpull from flow over/under gate

applicability: Hoist capacity: F_design = 1.5 × F_hoist (USACE). Downpull can be significant for high-head gates — requires hydraulic model or CFD analysis. Gate closing force: W × sin(θ) must exceed friction and uplift (or add closing weight).

title: Radial Gate Discharge Coefficient (Toch Correlation)

Cd.description: Discharge coefficient for radial gate underflow

Cc.description: Contraction coefficient (function of gate angle and opening ratio)

applicability: Cc depends on the angle of the gate lip with the flow direction. Typical Cd range: 0.60–0.72. More detailed: Cd = f(d/H₁, θ_lip) from USACE HDC charts or Toch (1955) relationships.

title: Cavitation Index for Gate/Valve

V_ref.description: Reference velocity (typically mean velocity in conduit upstream of gate)

applicability: Compare σ to σ_incipient for the specific gate type. If σ < σ_incipient → cavitation occurs. σ_incipient values: slide gate 0.5–2.0, radial gate 0.2–0.8, butterfly valve 0.2–1.5 (varies with opening).

title: Valve Flow Coefficient (Cv)

SG.description: Specific gravity of fluid (1.0 for water)

applicability: Standard valve sizing method. Cv is a function of valve type, size, and percent open. Relates to K (loss coefficient) by: K = 890 × d⁴ / Cv² (d in inches). SI equivalent: Kv = 0.865 × Cv.

title: Air Demand Behind High-Head Gate

β.description: Air demand ratio (air flow / water flow)

Fr.description: Froude number of flow downstream of gate

applicability: For conduit gates discharging as free jets. Air supply must be provided through air vents to prevent negative pressure in conduit downstream of gate. Vent pipe sized for β with velocity ≤ 45 m/s in air vent.

title: Spillway Gate — Regulated Discharge

Q.description: Discharge through partially opened spillway gate

H₂.description: Head at bottom of gate (H₁ - gate opening)

applicability: For partially opened radial or vertical-lift gates on spillway crests. When gate is fully open, reverts to standard weir equation. Cd varies with gate opening ratio and gate geometry — use USACE HDC charts for specific configurations.
